newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere A plunges in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere A plunges in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere A shares continued falling on Thursday amid heavy supply on the Beirut Stock Exchange and brokers said an announcement of the company's dividend was unlikely to take place soon.
A shares fell for the second consecutive day to $10.5 from $11 while B shares rose to $11.375 from $11.
Demand for A shares was 23,733 against a supply of 222,629 on Thursday's first fixing.

A surge in Solidere Global Depositary Receipts in London and an expected announcement of dividend at a Solidere shareholders' assembly scheduled for May 27, took the shares up to their 16-month highs before last weekend.

"There will be no quorum on the scheduled date, so the dividend declaration will be suspended at least three weeks. The market relaxed on this expectation," Nabil Aoun, head of brokers for Fidus, said.
"I think A share is at its minimum now but it will improve within two weeks," he added.
Official sources in Solidere supported Aoun's expectations.

"I doubt that there will be a quorum on the scheduled date, and this is normal in a big company like Solidere. I expect the next assembly to take place towards the end of June," a company official told Reuters.
The three listed banks, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce Banque Audi and Bank of Beirut, held steady at $16.25, $20, and $3.5625 respectively.
A total of 10,000 BOB shares changed hands in a block on the floor at $3.5625.
The LIBX bank index held steady at 136.71. The LISPI general index fell 0.12 percent to 86.54 and the BLOM general index fell 1.38 percent to 940.32.
Total BSE turnover fell sharply to 140,280 shares for a value of $1,317,272 from 216,164 shares for a value of $1,859,785 on Wednesday.
There was no trade in the four listed industrial companies: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
